findings.title: Delete cached data never refreshes the connected-calendars query
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation only calls onSuccess (the caller's onChanged). It does not invalidate trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the Remove App mutation at lines 53-65, which invalidates in onSettled. The wrapper is used in two places. CalendarListContainer passes onChanged, which invalidates connectedCalendars (apps/web/components/apps/CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88, 112-117). EventAdvancedTab renders SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper without onChanged (packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-377). On the event-type tab the success toast fires, but the 'Last updated' row and the Delete action stay on screen, and a second click succeeds again. Fix: invalidate connectedCalendars in the deleteCache onSuccess. utils is declared at line 52, after this mutation, so move it above.
findings.originReason: The component and the deleteCache mutation are new in this diff.

verification.reason: The deleteCache mutation only calls the optional onSuccess and never invalidates connectedCalendars. EventAdvancedTab renders SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper without onChanged, so on that tab the query stays stale after a delete.

findings.title: Pre-existing cache rows are stamped with the deploy time
findings.body: ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT NOW() gives every existing CalendarCache row the migration time. getCacheStatusByCredentialIds takes MAX(updatedAt) per credential (packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:179-186). A credential whose cache has not been rewritten since the deploy therefore shows 'Last updated: <deploy date>' while the data is older. Rows written by upsertCachedAvailability have expiresAt = write time + 30 days (calendar-cache.repository.ts:15-16, 157-168), so backfilling updatedAt = expiresAt - interval '30 days' for existing rows would be accurate. Alternatively, leave the column nullable for legacy rows so they show no timestamp. The header comment (lines 2-4) also says the column is added 'without a default value', which contradicts line 9.
findings.originReason: The migration is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The migration adds updatedAt NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing row gets the deploy time. getCacheStatusByCredentialIds takes _max.updatedAt, which then shows the deploy date for legacy caches. The header comment also contradicts the statement.

findings.title: Cache status bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
findings.body: Every sibling caller goes through CalendarCache.init(null) (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:463, 616, 981), which returns CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when the global calendar-cache flag is off (packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-28). This handler calls new CalendarCacheRepository() directly. With the flag off, the settings page still reads and shows stale cache rows and offers Delete cached data. The new mock method (calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-30) is never reached from here. Also, a throw from groupBy is not caught, so the whole connectedCalendars query fails and the cache badge can break the calendar list. Either use the gate, or state that the status is meant to show regardless of the flag, and catch the error.
findings.originReason: The cache-status lookup was added to the handler by this diff.

verification.reason: The handler constructs CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of going through CalendarCache.init, which returns the mock when the global flag is off. The groupBy call is not wrapped, so if it throws, the whole connectedCalendars query fails.

findings.title: ENV_FILE is resolved against the working directory
findings.body: ENV_FILE="../.env" is relative to the current directory. When run from the repository root, it writes to the parent directory (touch creates it if missing), not the root .env that the app reads. The script still prints 'Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in ../.env', so the webhook URL silently does not change. The path only points at the repo .env when the script runs from scripts/. Resolve it from the script's own location (for example, dirname of $0 plus /../.env). I found no usage doc that states the working directory.
findings.originReason: The script is new in this diff.

verification.reason: ENV_FILE="../.env" resolves against the caller's current directory, not the script's location. No usage doc or reference to the script exists in the repo.

findings.title: Reused tmole session takes its URL from a log this run did not create
findings.body: When tmole is already running, the URL is read from /tmp/tmole.log (line 30), which this run did not create. If that log is left from an earlier session, its URL may belong to a dead tunnel. The stale URL is then written to GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL (lines 67-71), and the script still prints 'Tunnelmole is running'. Read the log only when this run started tmole (OWNED_PID=true), or check that the URL is live.
findings.originReason: The script is new in this diff.

verification.reason: In the reuse branch, the URL comes from /tmp/tmole.log with no check that this log belongs to the running tmole process. A leftover log would supply a stale URL, which is then written to the env file.

findings.title: Failure paths exit 0 and sed -i '' is macOS-only
findings.body: cleanup() always exits 0 (line 17). That covers the rate-limit branch (line 49) and the 'Failed to extract URL' branch (line 58), so callers and CI see success on failure. Line 68 uses sed -i '', which is BSD syntax and fails on Linux. Exit non-zero on the failure paths and document the script as macOS-only, or use a portable form.
findings.originReason: The script is new in this diff.

verification.reason: cleanup() always runs exit 0, and the rate-limit and missing-URL failure paths both call it. sed -i '' is BSD syntax; GNU sed reads '' as the script and fails.

findings.title: dev:cron runs an undeclared, unpinned tsx through npx
findings.body: dev:cron now runs npx tsx cron-tester.ts. tsx is not declared in apps/web/package.json or the root package.json, so each run fetches whatever version npx resolves, outside the lockfile. ts-node is still declared and used by other scripts in this file (lines 24-25, 196). Add tsx as a pinned devDependency, or keep ts-node. The PR body records the change but not the reason.
findings.originReason: The diff changed dev:cron from ts-node to npx tsx.

verification.reason: dev:cron now runs npx tsx, but no package.json in the repo declares tsx. ts-node is still a declared devDependency.

findings.title: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is written but nothing in the change reads it
findings.body: Each cache refresh, including the Google webhook path (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/webhook.ts:42-46), now issues an UPDATE on every SelectedCalendar row of the credential. The settings UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt instead (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-36). A text search of packages/ found no reader of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Either drop the write or name the reader. Otherwise it adds one write per webhook for nothing.
findings.originReason: The write was added by this diff.

verification.reason: The new updateManyByCredentialId(..., {}) call only exists to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. A search of packages found no code that reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt. The only other mention is a type Pick in getConnectedDestinationCalendars.

findings.title: disableConnectionModification now gates the error card and does not gate cache deletion
findings.body: Before: the error card (second block) hid Remove only when delegationCredentialId was set. The first block also hid it for disableConnectionModification. The shared dropdown now applies disableConnectionModification to both blocks (SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:129-130), so Remove disappears from error cards in event-type settings. Meanwhile Delete cached data is shown where disableConnectionModification is true (EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375 passes true), so the flag no longer means 'no changes' there. Neither change is in the PR description. Confirm both are intended.
findings.originReason: The diff replaced DisconnectIntegration with the shared dropdown and changed the gating.

verification.reason: In the base, the error Alert hid Remove only for delegation credentials. The head passes disableConnectionModification to the Alert's dropdown, so Remove is now hidden there too. Delete cached data stays visible even when disableConnectionModification is true, which is how EventAdvancedTab renders it.

findings.title: No test covers the ownership check on a destructive handler
findings.body: The only guard before deleteMany is the findFirst at lines 17-26, which checks that the credential belongs to the user. No test in this change covers it: that another user's credentialId is rejected and their cache rows are untouched. The new groupBy method and the connectedCalendars enrichment are also untested.
findings.originReason: The handler and the repository method are new in this diff.

verification.reason: No test or spec file in the head references deleteCache or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, so the ownership check is untested.

findings.title: Date is hard-coded to en-US
findings.body: Intl.DateTimeFormat is fixed to 'en-US' (line 89), while the rest of the dropdown is localized through t(). Users in other locales get English date order and 12-hour time. Use the app's current locale instead.
findings.originReason: The component is new in this diff.

verification.reason: Intl.DateTimeFormat is hard-coded to 'en-US', while the surrounding strings go through t() from useLocale.

findings.title: 'cannot be undone' overstates the delete
findings.body: The cached data is derived. Deleting it forces a refetch, and no user data is lost. The string should say that the cache is cleared and rebuilt on the next check.
findings.originReason: The string was added by this diff.

verification.reason: The deleted rows are derived availability cache that upsertCachedAvailability rebuilds on the next fetch, so 'cannot be undone' overstates the effect.

contracts.action: Delete cached data (deleteCache mutation, confirmed in dialog)
contracts.before_after: Remove invalidates connectedCalendars and apps.integrations on settle. Delete cache calls only onSuccess (the caller's onChanged) and invalidates nothing.
contracts.visible_effect: On the installed-calendars page, onChanged invalidates connectedCalendars, so the status row and action update. On the event-type advanced tab, onChanged is not passed, so after the success toast the status row and action stay until remount.
contracts.failure_mode: Mutation error shows 'Error deleting cache' and changes nothing. Success on an already-empty cache is still reported as success.

contracts.before_after: DisconnectIntegration disables the action when isDelegationCredential({credentialId}) and passes an optional teamId. The new code checks only delegationCredentialId and never sends teamId.
contracts.visible_effect: For DB delegation credentials the action is hidden, same as before. For in-memory delegation credentials the guard depends on delegationCredentialId being set.
contracts.failure_mode: If the guard is missed, the server call fails and an error toast shows. Nothing is lost.
contracts.open_question: Do in-memory delegation credentials always carry delegatedToId, so that delegationCredentialId is non-null for them?

contracts.equivalent_path: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-28 (CalendarCache.init feature gate used by all other callers)
contracts.before_after: Siblings get the repository via the global-flag gate, which returns the mock when off. The new code constructs CalendarCacheRepository directly and always queries.
contracts.visible_effect: With the flag off, stale cache badges and the Delete action still show. With the flag on, the badge shows MAX(updatedAt) per credential.
contracts.failure_mode: The groupBy has no catch. A DB error rejects the whole connectedCalendars query, so the calendar settings list fails to load.

contracts.before_after: The sibling reads one row by the unique key. The new code aggregates over many credentials in one query with an IN filter on credentialId.
contracts.visible_effect: Credentials with no cache rows are absent from the map and get null, so the badge and Delete action are hidden.
contracts.failure_mode: Rejection propagates to the connectedCalendars query (see the connectedCalendars entry).

contracts.action: deleteCache: destructive deleteMany of all CalendarCache rows for one credential
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:955 (unwatch clears the cache with deleteMany by credentialId)
contracts.before_after: Sibling deletes by credentialId with no ownership check, since it runs server-side after unwatch. The new path checks ownership with findFirst immediately before the delete, in the same call.
contracts.visible_effect: Cache rows for that credential are removed. The next availability request misses and refetches.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejection surfaces as an error toast. Cache rows are derived, so nothing needs a retry journal and nothing is orphaned. The delete is scoped to one credentialId.

contracts.action: updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) after cache refresh (also runs on the Google webhook path)
contracts.before_after: The sibling writes CalendarCache.updatedAt through the repository. The new code writes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for every row of the credential, across all event types.
contracts.visible_effect: None in this change. The UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt. A text search of packages/ found no reader of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.
contracts.failure_mode: If fetchAvailability throws, the loop stops and the update is skipped. The webhook handler (webhook.ts:46) propagates the error. Stale updatedAt on SelectedCalendar is harmless because nothing reads it.

contracts.action: Schema and migration: CalendarCache.updatedAt added with DEFAULT now()
contracts.before_after: Before the migration, the table has no updatedAt. The migration backfills every existing row with the migration time. New rows and upserts set updatedAt to write time via @updatedAt.
contracts.visible_effect: Credentials whose cache has not been rewritten since the deploy show the deploy date as 'Last updated'.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong timestamp in the UI. No data loss.

contracts.action: dev/test script writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL into an env file
contracts.before_after: No equivalent in the repo. Writes ../.env relative to the current directory, creating it if missing.
contracts.visible_effect: Prints success and names ../.env. The app reads the repo root .env, so the URL does not change there when run from the root.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent misconfiguration of the Google webhook URL. Also see the reuse finding at line 30.

summary: Reviewed all 17 files in this part (none binary, none skipped). Most consequential: the Delete cached data action never refreshes connectedCalendars, so on the event-type advanced tab (which passes no onChanged) the cache row and action stay stale after a successful delete. The migration stamps every pre-existing CalendarCache row with the deploy time, which the UI then shows as 'Last updated'. The connectedCalendars handler skips the calendar-cache feature gate every sibling uses. The tunnelmole script resolves its env file against the working directory and can reuse a stale URL from /tmp/tmole.log. Smaller items: a hard-coded en-US date format, an unpinned npx tsx in dev:cron, an unread SelectedCalendar.updatedAt write, missing tests on the ownership check, and misleading 'cannot be undone' copy. Limits: I did not build or run anything. common.json was checked by reading the changed block and grepping for the key names, not read in full (3,388 lines). CalendarService.test.ts was checked only around the affected function. The in-memory delegation question is open and depends on CalendarManager's credential construction.
